key_insight: StreamCacheVGGT replaces destructive binary token eviction with a training-free cache manager that uses cross-layer robust scoring and hybrid compression to preserve useful geometry information from video streams, enabling stable dense 3D reconstruction under a fixed memory budget.
problem_solved: Existing O(1) streaming frameworks for continuous 3D reconstruction destroy information by evicting tokens outright and rely on noisy, single-layer scoring; this yields unstable, low-quality geometry when memory is constrained. StreamCacheVGGT addresses these failures to maintain reconstruction quality and temporal consistency within constant memory limits.
method: Training-free cache management with two synergistic modules: (a) cross-layer robust scoring that aggregates multi-layer and temporal signals to rank token importance, reducing evaluation noise; (b) hybrid cache compression that compresses/merges low-importance tokens (e.g., quantization, residual pooling, token fusion) instead of binary deletion to retain salient information.

Streaming pipeline that integrates with existing Visual Geometry Transformers (VGGT) to perform on-the-fly cache updates and inference while keeping memory O(1), improving temporal stability and reconstruction fidelity without retraining.
Design choices emphasize low compute overhead and plug-and-play deployment: lightweight scoring aggregation, selective lossy compression, and occasional full-state refreshes to avoid drift.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, plug-and-play solution to run high-quality, temporally stable dense 3D reconstruction from video on memory-limited platforms, improving inference robustness and deployment feasibility for real-time and edge applications.
